reason: Examined def-left-haar-integral-and-left-haar-measure, lem-haar-measure-is-positive-on-nonempty-open-sets-and-finite-on-compact-sets. Let μ be any nonzero left Haar measure on R. The open interval (0,1) has c=μ((0,1))>0 by Haar full support. Its translates (2n,2n+1), n≥0, are pairwise disjoint and each has mass c by translation invariance. Countable additivity gives μ(R)≥Σn≥0c=∞. Thus no scalar rescaling makes μ(R)=1; compactness is exactly what allowed normalized finite averaging. No choice is used once a nonzero Haar measure is given; the example does not claim Haar nonexistence.
